atlanticbluefintuna: An Atlantic bluefin tuna, a massive torpedo-shaped fish built like a muscle, deepest just behind the head and tapering to a very narrow tail stalk carrying a STIFF CRESCENT-SHAPED TAIL. Its back is metallic dark blue and its flanks brilliant silver, and A ROW OF SMALL SEPARATE YELLOW FINLETS runs along the top and bottom edges between the second fin and the tail. Short side fins fold flat into grooves.
atlanticherring: An Atlantic herring, a SLIM SILVER FISH about the length of a hand, flattened side to side, with a single small back fin set halfway along, a deeply forked tail, LARGE ROUND DARK EYES for its size, and a slightly projecting lower jaw. Its back is steel blue-green and its flanks are bare mirror-silver with a faint keel of scales along the belly.
chubmackerel: A chub mackerel, a small streamlined spindle-shaped fish with a pointed snout and a narrow tail stalk, its back METALLIC BLUE-GREEN CROSSED BY MANY WAVY DARK VERTICAL BARS that break up over silvery flanks. Two separate fins along its back, A ROW OF SMALL SEPARATE FINLETS between the rear fin and the tail, and a stiff forked tail.
mahimahi: A mahi-mahi, a long compressed brilliantly coloured fish, GOLDEN-YELLOW ALONG THE FLANKS scattered with fine iridescent blue-green flecks and deep electric blue along the back. Its BACK FIN IS A SINGLE LONG CREST RUNNING FROM JUST BEHIND THE HEAD ALL THE WAY TO THE TAIL, and the adult male's forehead is a STEEP BLUNT VERTICAL WALL, almost square in profile.
opah: An Opah, a huge DEEP ROUND DISC-SHAPED FISH, nearly as tall as it is long and flattened side to side like a great plate. Its body is deep rose and steel blue-grey, SPRINKLED ALL OVER WITH SMALL WHITE SPOTS, and every fin, along with its small mouth and the ring around its LARGE GOLD-RIMMED EYE, is BRIGHT CRIMSON-SCARLET.
oceanicwhitetipshark: An oceanic whitetip shark, a stocky shark with a short rounded snout and the marking that names it: its FINS ARE VERY LONG, BROAD AND ROUNDED AT THE TIPS, and the tip of each large fin is MOTTLED WHITE, as though dipped in paint. Its enormously long paddle-shaped pectoral fins are held out stiffly to the sides. Bronze-grey above, pale below.
blueshark: A blue shark, a SLENDER GRACEFUL SHARK with a very long conical pointed snout, LARGE DARK ROUND EYES, and EXTREMELY LONG NARROW SCYTHE-LIKE PECTORAL FINS held out like blades. Its back is a vivid deep INDIGO BLUE fading through bright blue on the flanks to a sharply demarcated snow-white belly. Its tail has a long sweeping upper lobe.
remora: A remora, a slim dark grey fish with the feature that identifies it: THE TOP OF ITS HEAD IS A LARGE FLAT OVAL SUCKING DISC, ridged across with many parallel movable slats like the sole of a shoe, occupying the whole upper surface of the head and reaching back past the eyes. Its lower jaw juts out beyond the upper, and its body tapers to a small forked tail.
sargassumfrogfish: A sargassum frogfish, a small squat rounded fish whose entire body is BROKEN UP BY MANY RAGGED FLESHY TASSELS, FRINGES AND WEED-LIKE FLAPS OF SKIN growing directly out of it in every direction, mottled olive, gold and white with dark scribbled lines and pale spots. Its front fins are ARM-LIKE WITH ELBOW-LIKE JOINTS AND SPLAYED FINGERS, and its mouth is huge and upturned.
humboldtsquid: A Humboldt squid, a large powerful muscular squid with a thick conical mantle, two broad triangular fins at the rear, and EIGHT STOUT ARMS PLUS TWO LONGER TENTACLES held together in a spreading cone. Its suckers are ringed with SHARP TOOTHED CHITIN RINGS. Its skin is flushing in bold irregular patches of DEEP RED AND CREAM-WHITE at once, and it has large dark eyes.
portuguesemanowar: A Portuguese man o' war, a floating COLONY that reads as one animal: a smooth translucent GAS-FILLED FLOAT SHAPED LIKE A LONG PASTEL BLUE-PINK BUBBLE with a THIN RUFFLED CREST STANDING UP ALONG ITS TOP EDGE like a sail, and beneath it a dense hanging bundle of many BRIGHT BLUE TENTACLES of wildly different lengths, some short and frilled, one or two immensely long and fine. Absolutely NOT a ship.
loggerheadturtle: A loggerhead sea turtle swimming, a sea turtle with an ENORMOUS BLOCKY WIDE HEAD, disproportionately large for its body, carrying a heavy hooked beak and thick jaw muscles. Its heart-shaped shell is REDDISH-BROWN and slightly ridged, its neck and flippers are warm yellow-brown, and its front flippers are long and paddle-shaped with a single visible claw.
oliveridleyturtle: An olive ridley sea turtle swimming, a SMALL sea turtle with a nearly ROUND HEART-SHAPED SHELL that is high-domed and a plain uniform OLIVE-GREEN, its rim carrying MORE THAN FIVE PAIRED PLATES down each side, more than other sea turtles. Its head is moderate and triangular, and its front flippers are broad paddles with one or two small claws.
northerngannet: A northern gannet in flight, a large brilliant WHITE seabird with LONG SLENDER POINTED WINGS TIPPED WITH SHARP BLACK, a warm BUTTERSCOTCH-YELLOW WASH over the head and nape, and a long stout pale blue-grey DAGGER BILL coming to a fine point. Its eye is pale and staring, ringed with a fine line of bare blue skin, and its tail is pointed.
sootyshearwater: A sooty shearwater in flight, a slender seabird UNIFORMLY DARK CHOCOLATE-BROWN all over, with VERY LONG NARROW STIFF WINGS held straight and slightly bowed, and a SILVERY PALE FLASH ALONG THE CENTRE OF THE UNDERWING. Its bill is long, slim and dark with a hooked tip and TUBULAR NOSTRILS RIDGED ALONG THE TOP. Short tail, small dark feet.
wilsonsstormpetrel: A Wilson's storm petrel, a TINY sooty-black seabird ABOUT THE SIZE OF A SPARROW, with short rounded wings, a SQUARE-ENDED TAIL, and a BRIGHT CLEAN WHITE BAND ACROSS ITS RUMP. Its legs are very long and slender for its size, trailing beyond the tail, and its FEET CARRY SMALL BRIGHT YELLOW PATCHES between the toes. Small black tube-nosed bill.
redbilledtropicbird: A red-billed tropicbird in flight, a brilliant white seabird finely BARRED WITH BLACK ACROSS ITS BACK, with a bold BLACK STRIPE THROUGH EACH EYE, black outer wing feathers, a stout slightly downcurved CORAL-RED BILL, and the feature that names it: TWO EXTREMELY LONG THIN WHITE TAIL STREAMERS trailing far behind, together longer than the rest of the bird.
